extracted.intended_audience: Referees/reviewers for the American Economic Review (AER)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for referees reviewing manuscripts submitted to the American Economic Review, covering anonymity, conflict-of-interest handling, procedural submission, and suggested external reading on writing referee reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind review / referee anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to the American Economic Review are reviewed in a single-blind fashion. Because the referee(s) should remain anonymous to authors, we ask you not to use your name in the body or filename of your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include your name anywhere in the text of your report or in the filename you upload. Maintain anonymity to authors throughout the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest disclosures — do not base recommendations on conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscript submissions are accompanied by individual disclosure statements from each coauthor. However, recommendations should not be based on whether potential conflicts of interest exist, but on whether the conclusions in the paper are robust, credible, and worthy of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although disclosure statements are provided, evaluate the manuscript on its merits (robustness, credibility, publication-worthiness) rather than on the mere existence of disclosed conflicts. If a conflict affects your ability to review, follow the journal's conflict procedures (implied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core evaluation standards: robustness, credibility, and publication-worthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations should be based on whether the conclusions in the paper are robust, credible, and worthy of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming a recommendation, focus on (and document) the credibility of results, the robustness of methods/empirical checks, and whether the contribution meets the journal's bar for publication. Use concrete critiques and suggestions tied to these dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the AEA ScholarOne submission/review system
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEA uses ScholarOne Manuscripts for submission and peer review tracking. To see more information and instructions for submitting a review, log in and navigate to your Reviewer Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit reviews and follow procedural instructions via the ScholarOne Reviewer Center. Check the system for any journal-specific forms or required answer fields when completing your report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult recommended external referee-report guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage you to read the brief set of guidelines on referee reports prepared by Econometrica and the more detailed guidelines published in the Journal of Economic Perspectives by Jonathan Berk, Campbell Harvey, and David Hirshleifer. These guidelines do not represent official AEA policy, but you may find them helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These external documents contain helpful advice and templates on writing referee reports; consider them for structure and best practices, while following any AER-specific requirements in ScholarOne and this page.
